name: MAX31865 PT100 RTD amplifier
description: Analog Devices (Maxim) MAX31865 resistance-to-digital converter for platinum RTDs (PT100/PT1000): 15-bit ratiometric ADC reading RTD resistance against a precision reference resistor, with fault detection, over SPI (modes 1 and 3). Chip runs on 3.0-3.6 V; the breakout has a regulator and level shifting for 3-5 V. Sold as: Adafruit PT100 RTD Temperature Sensor Amplifier - MAX31865 (product 3328), 8-pin header VIN, GND, 3V3, CLK, SDO, SDI, CS, RDY, 430 ohm 0.1% reference resistor, 2/3/4-wire RTD terminal blocks (4-wire by default).
eli5: Reads a platinum temperature probe very precisely by measuring its resistance, which rises as it gets hotter.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply 3-5 V into the on-board 3.3 V regulator; use the same voltage as your logic (3.3 V on ESP32/Pico)

pins.name: 3V3
pins.description: 3.3 V output of the on-board regulator (up to 100 mA); not a supply input, leave unconnected

pins.name: CLK
pins.description: SPI clock into the MAX31865 (up to 5 MHz, SPI mode 1 or 3)

pins.name: SDO
pins.description: SPI data out of the MAX31865 (to the board's MISO)

pins.name: SDI
pins.description: SPI data into the MAX31865 (from the board's MOSI); needed to write the configuration register

pins.name: CS
pins.description: Chip select, active low; a 1-shot conversion starts when CS goes high

pins.name: RDY
pins.description: DRDY data-ready output, active low; optional (the driver waits the conversion time instead)

supplierQuery: MAX31865 PT100 RTD amplifier breakout SPI
buildNotes: SPI mode 1 (polarity=0, phase=1) or mode 3; registers are read at 0Xh and written at 8Xh.
1-shot reading: write 0x80 to config (VBIAS on), wait ~10 ms, write 0xA0 (VBIAS + 1-shot), wait 52 ms (60 Hz filter) or 62.5 ms (50 Hz), then read registers 01h-02h.
RTD data is a 15-bit code in bits 15..1; bit 0 is the fault flag. RRTD = code x RREF / 32768, with RREF = 430 ohm on the Adafruit PT100 board (4300 ohm on the PT1000 version).
Convert resistance to temperature with the Callendar-Van Dusen equation (A = 3.9083e-3, B = -5.775e-7, C = -4.183e-12 below 0 C).
The board ships set for 4-wire RTDs. For 2- or 3-wire probes, bridge/cut the solder jumpers as Adafruit describes and pass wires=3 to the driver for a 3-wire probe.
Leave 3V3 unconnected: it is the regulator's output, not an input.

driver.code:
# MAX31865 RTD-to-digital converter (Analog Devices / Maxim), MicroPython driver.
# Written from datasheet 19-6478 Rev 3: SPI mode 1 or 3 (CPHA = 1), read address 0Xh, write 8Xh,
# 1-shot conversion with VBIAS switched on beforehand, RRTD = ADC code x RREF / 2^15,
# temperature from the IEC 751 Callendar-Van Dusen equation.
from machine import Pin
import math
import time

_CONFIG = 0x00
_RTD_MSB = 0x01
_FAULT = 0x07

_BIAS = 0x80
_ONE_SHOT = 0x20
_THREE_WIRE = 0x10
_FAULT_CLEAR = 0x02
_FILTER_50HZ = 0x01

# IEC 751 Callendar-Van Dusen coefficients (datasheet)
_A = 3.90830e-3
_B = -5.77500e-7
_C = -4.18301e-12


class MAX31865:
    def __init__(self, spi, cs, rref=430.0, r0=100.0, wires=4, filter_hz=60):
        """spi: machine.SPI in mode 1 (polarity=0, phase=1), up to 5 MHz.
        cs: GPIO number of CS. rref: reference resistor (430 ohm on the Adafruit PT100 board,
        4300 ohm on the PT1000 version). r0: RTD resistance at 0 C (100 for PT100).
        wires: 2, 3 or 4 (3 needs the board's 3-wire jumpers too). filter_hz: 50 or 60 (mains notch)."""
        self.spi = spi
        self.cs = Pin(cs, Pin.OUT, value=1)
        self.rref = rref
        self.r0 = r0
        self._cfg = (_THREE_WIRE if wires == 3 else 0) | (_FILTER_50HZ if filter_hz == 50 else 0)
        self._conv_ms = 63 if filter_hz == 50 else 52  # 62.5 ms / 52 ms single conversion
        self._write(_CONFIG, self._cfg)  # normally-off, VBIAS off

    def _write(self, reg, val):
        self.cs.value(0)
        self.spi.write(bytes([0x80 | reg, val & 0xFF]))
        self.cs.value(1)

    def _read(self, reg, n):
        buf = bytearray(n + 1)
        self.cs.value(0)
        self.spi.write_readinto(bytes([reg & 0x7F]) + bytes(n), buf)
        self.cs.value(1)
        return buf[1:]

    def fault(self):
        """Fault Status register (07h): D7 RTD high, D6 RTD low, D5..D3 REFIN/RTDIN, D2 over/undervoltage."""
        return self._read(_FAULT, 1)[0]

    def clear_fault(self):
        # Fault Status Clear with D5, D3 and D2 written as 0 (datasheet).
        self._write(_CONFIG, self._cfg | _FAULT_CLEAR)

    def read_raw(self):
        """Run one 1-shot conversion and return the 15-bit ADC code (RRTD / RREF x 32768)."""
        self.clear_fault()
        self._write(_CONFIG, self._cfg | _BIAS)
        time.sleep_ms(10)  # input RC filter settling: >= 10.5 time constants + 1 ms
        self._write(_CONFIG, self._cfg | _BIAS | _ONE_SHOT)  # conversion starts when CS goes high
        time.sleep_ms(self._conv_ms + 3)
        d = self._read(_RTD_MSB, 2)
        self._write(_CONFIG, self._cfg)  # VBIAS off between readings
        raw = (d[0] << 8) | d[1]
        if raw & 1:
            f = self.fault()
            self.clear_fault()
            raise OSError('MAX31865 fault 0x%02X: check the RTD wiring' % f)
        return raw >> 1

    def resistance(self):
        """RTD resistance in ohms: ADC code x RREF / 2^15."""
        return self.read_raw() * self.rref / 32768

    def temperature(self, r=None):
        """Temperature in C from the Callendar-Van Dusen equation (exact inverse for T >= 0 C,
        Newton iteration including the C term below 0 C)."""
        if r is None:
            r = self.resistance()
        t = (-_A + math.sqrt(_A * _A - 4 * _B * (1 - r / self.r0))) / (2 * _B)
        if t >= 0:
            return t
        for _ in range(8):
            f = self.r0 * (1 + _A * t + _B * t * t + _C * (t - 100) * t ** 3) - r
            df = self.r0 * (_A + 2 * _B * t + _C * (4 * t ** 3 - 300 * t * t))
            t -= f / df
        return t

    def read(self):
        """Measure once and return (resistance in ohms, temperature in C)."""
        r = self.resistance()
        return r, self.temperature(r)

example.code:
from machine import Pin, SoftSPI
import time
from max31865 import MAX31865

# SoftSPI works on any pins of an ESP32 or Pico; the MAX31865 needs SPI mode 1 (phase=1)
spi = SoftSPI(baudrate=1000000, polarity=0, phase=1, sck=Pin({CLK}), mosi=Pin({SDI}), miso=Pin({SDO}))
rtd = MAX31865(spi, {CS}, rref=430.0, r0=100.0, wires=4)  # Adafruit PT100 board: RREF = 430 ohm
while True:
    r, t = rtd.read()
    print('R=%.2f T=%.2fC' % (r, t))
    time.sleep(1)
